subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Shape-Memory Alloys: Metals That Remember
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Shape-Memory Alloys: Metals That Remember.

hook.text: Bend a nickel-titanium wire. Heat it up. It snaps back to its original shape — every time.

buildup.text: Shape-memory alloys switch between two crystal structures at different temperatures. One is stiff, one is flexible.

discovery.text: The alloy 'remembers' the shape it was trained in. Heating triggers a phase change that restores it.

twist.text: Heart stents use nitinol. Compressed for insertion, they expand to body temperature and hold arteries open.

climax.text: NASA tested shape-memory alloy tires for Mars rovers. They deform over rocks and spring back instantly.

punchline.text: A metal with a memory. Heat it and it comes home.

quiz.question: How do shape-memory alloys return to their original shape?
options: An electric current forces atoms back into alignment
Heating triggers a crystal phase change that restores the trained shape
They contain springs inside the metal that pull it back
